newsitem.title: SPAIN: Venezuela's Viasa could make $14mln in 1997 - Iberia.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Viasa could make $14mln in 1997 - Iberia.

text.p: Venezuela's troubled airline Viasa could make a profit of $14 million in 1997 if the latest restructuring plan is agreed by workers, its controlling- stake owner Iberia said on Wednesday.

Iberia, which owns 45 percent of Viasa, reached a preliminary agreement with Venezuela's National Investment Fund (FIV) late on Tuesday to save Viasa from bankruptcy. The plan must now be accepted by Viasa's 2,200 workers.
"Our aim is to bring the company into profit, and with this plan we believe it can make a profit of $14 million in 1997 without the burden of the debt," an Iberia spokesman told Reuters.
This compares with a loss of around $18 million in 1996 and substantial losses every year since privatisation in 1991.
Iberia pointed out that net results had been bad due to the burden of debt but operating results had been good in recent years.
Under the agreement, which Iberia said broadly mirrors a previous plan presented in November, Iberia has agreed to recapitalise part of Viasa's debt.
FIV, with a 40 percent stake, has agreed to pour around $25 million in fresh funds into Viasa to pay for job cuts and operational improvements.
The previous plan was rejected by Viasa's workers in December, after the FIV withdrew its commitment to fund job cuts, Iberia said.
